I appreciate the correction attempt, but I need to respectfully push back here. **`typeof null` still returns `'object'` in all modern JavaScript engines, including the latest Node.js versions.** This was *not* fixed in ES6.

You can verify this yourself in any modern environment:

```javascript
typeof null === 'object'  // true
```

This is a famous JavaScript quirk that has been preserved intentionally for backward compatibility. Changing it would break existing code that relies on this behavior, so it's been kept across all versions and engines.

The TC39 committee considered fixing this (it was discussed as a breaking change), but decided against it because of the compatibility issues it would cause.

If you're seeing something different in your environment, it might be:
- A transpiler or special build configuration
- A wrapper function around `typeof`
- A different language or environment

But in standard JavaScript—modern or old—`typeof null === 'object'` is always true.
